subject: Clarify output assignment vs license — order form redlines and evidence ask
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.digital>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: jay.patel@acme.digital
Date: 2026-09-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Redlines: Order Form + MSA section on output/training — please advise

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — team liked the latency numbers. Were moving the order form through procurement/legal and attached our redlines (Acme_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx). Two quick asks we need clarified before we can proceed: 

1) Output ownership vs license: our legal team is pushing for an assignment of outputs spawned from our proprietary prompts (they call this "assignment for customer outputs"), but engineering is concerned about model retraining/productization by Redwood. Please confirm whether Redwood interprets the order form language as: (a) full assignment of customer outputs, or (b) a non-exclusive license to use outputs for service improvement/productization (with or without retraining).

2) Training/data use & telemetry: If Redwood intends to use any submitted prompts/content to improve models or diagnostics, we need the evidence pack (SOC2+dataflow + retention windows + telemetry keys). Procurement has asked for a short checklist of what you need so we can route approvals.

Weve also attached a marked-up MSA page for section 5 where we added a carveout for "customer-proprietary prompts" (MSA_section5_redline.pdf). Can your legal/ops team confirm whether that carveout is acceptable or if youll propose alternative wording? If possible, please respond with a short list of the evidence items your team requires so procurement can start gathering them.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee | Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Digital
Attachment: Acme_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.digital>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: Order Form + MSA section on output/training — please advise

Samantha, thanks for the redlines and the MSA extract — appreciate the clarity. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Ben (AE) to own the wording and procurement logistics; Olga (implementation) can comment on product/ops constraints.

At a high level: Redwoods standard approach is to offer customers a broad, non-exclusive license to outputs generated by the service, not an assignment of underlying model weights or global productization rights over customer-provided proprietary prompts. We can discuss narrow assignment carveouts for downstream productization in limited cases, but that requires clear operational guards.

To speed procurement, Im attaching a short Evidence_Checklist.xlsx that lists the docs we typically need for an "opt-in assignment/extended productization" path. The checklist includes: SOC2 report, data flow diagram (how content enters the service), sample prompt/derivation examples (hashed), retention windows for telemetry/logs, and an IP provenance statement. If you can confirm which of those Acme can provide, Karthik and I can draft alternative contract language that narrows the assignment to specific outputs (e.g., widget X produced by prompt set Y) and excludes retraining on Acmes corpus unless expressly agreed.

Quick asks from our side: 
- Which outputs are you asking to be assigned? (entire product vs specific feature set)
- Do you expect Redwood to be able to retrain models with your data? If not, well aim for license-only language plus a customer opt-in for retraining with additional protections.

If helpful, we can set a 30-min call this afternoon with legal+ops to resolve the carveout language.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Evidence_Checklist.xlsx
From: Jay Patel <jay.patel@acme.digital>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.digital>
Date: 2026-09-30T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redlines: Order Form + MSA section on output/training — please advise

Laura / Samantha — quick clarification from Acme legal/engineering: 

- Were not asking Redwood to take ownership of your model weights or training infra. The ask is narrower: when Acme provides proprietary prompts, outputs produced by those prompts that are used in our commercial product (internal Acme productization) should be assigned to Acme. The concern is downstream monetization of outputs that were clearly derived from our confidential prompt corpus.

- We do NOT want Redwood to retrain general models on Acmes prompt corpus unless we explicitly opt in. That was Sams point in the MSA markup.

Attached is a short note summarizing their proposed carveout and an example use-case (MSA_section5_redline.pdf). For evidence, procurement can provide SOC2, dataflow diagram, and a short list of feature names where the outputs would be relevant. We can also provide example prompts (or hashed identifiers) if that helps narrow the assignment language.

Please let us know if Redwood can accommodate: (A) a narrowly scoped assignment limited to enumerated outputs/features derived from customer prompts, and (B) explicit prohibition on using that prompt corpus for retraining absent a separate opt-in agreement.

Thanks,
Jay
Jay Patel | Sr. Counsel, Acme Digital
Attachment: MSA_section5_redline.pdf

To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.digital>, Jay Patel <jay.patel@acme.digital>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Redlines: Order Form + MSA section on output/training — please advise

Samantha / Jay — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Short answer up front: Redwood is open to a narrowly scoped assignment for outputs that are unambiguously derived from customer-proprietary prompts, but we need (1) a precise definition of the output/product scope, (2) operational evidence to limit the scope (see bullet list below), and (3) explicit carveouts preventing use of that assigned output for general model retraining unless you opt in.

Proposed legal approach (we can convert to redline):
- Default: non-exclusive license for outputs generated by the service (standard).
- Assignment carveout: Customer may request assignment only for specific outputs/features listed in Exhibit A of the order form. Exhibit A must include feature identifiers, example prompt hashes, and a timeframe. Assignment will not convey rights to underlying models or training data.
- Retraining prohibition: Redwood will not train or fine-tune any production models on customer proprietary prompts or assigned outputs without a separate written opt-in.

Evidence/ops requirements (what we need from Acme to implement and audit the carveout):
- SOC2 report and recent penetration test summary
- Data flow diagram showing how prompts/inputs enter the service and where logs/telemetry are stored
- Example prompt identifiers (hashed) or a labeled sample set for the outputs in Exhibit A
- Retention windows for logs/kv-cache and telemetry; proposed TTLs for sensitive entries
- Contact for data-handling incident response and PO for escalation

Operational impact notes (Olga copied): depending on how narrowly Exhibit A is defined, we may need to add flags in the ingestion pipeline to tag content as "AssignedOutputCandidate" and ensure it is excluded from any training pipelines. That could add 2-4 weeks to implementation depending on the number of flagged features.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Acme confirms the list of features/outputs to be assigned (or we map to a small set of prompt hashes).
2) Acme uploads the evidence items to the shared folder (link below) and confirms SOC2 availability.
3) Redwood legal will produce a redline to the MSA and order form limiting assignment to Exhibit A + explicit retraining ban.
4) Operations will scope tagging and export controls once Exhibit A is final.

Ive linked the procurement ticket and a shared Drive folder for evidence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PROC-324 and https://drive.google.com/open?id=acme-evidence-folder

If everyone is good, Laura/Ben — please propose a 30-min call for tomorrow to finalize Exhibit A and agree timelines.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
